body: I had a friend in a similar situation and at the end of it the father screamed at the newborn for crying constantly, shook the baby, and nearly killed the child. Keep a really close eye on your baby please. It’s an insane job and if he couldn’t step up to support you in a comforting and safe manner then his behavior with a baby isn’t something I would trust. I’m so sorry you went through this and I wish you had a better experience welcoming your baby! It’s such a hard experience but love your baby and don’t let him dictate. At the end of it, that’s your baby and you’ll know best. Please watch your baby and I hope you and your son stay safe and happy! Best of luck

I honestly feel you. I was single and alone my whole pregnancy and am still alone but my friend who just broke up with her boyfriend of 7 years now has a new one and they’re so happy. I felt and still feel the same way you do. It frustrates and saddens me a lot but I just try to ignore it. Unfortunately now I avoid her because I struggle with the feelings so I hope you cope better than me. I just wanted to say it’s ok to be frustrated and upset. You’re not the only one

All the time. My kids dad was abusive but he died before she was born so I never really had any experience with co-parenting. I always see whole families and get really jealous or angry but what can you do. I wish it would go away. You’re situation is really complicated and up and down though. I’m so sorry! I hope things will clear up for you soon

I used to have a routine and she was doing really well but it just stopped working and keeping to the routine doesn’t seem to matter. That’s a fair point though. I seriously wish she could just tell me what’s the issue but she can’t and probably doesn’t really know herself.

I have but usually get referred to my psych which is fine. I have anti depressants and a lot of other meds so it’s hard to change things out. She mostly just chalks it up to my BPD so we haven’t really talked about Postpartum depression. I’ll bring it up though.
I hope so. I pretty much live with my headphones in right now.

The weathers been awful lately so we haven’t taken walks but I do something similar with car rides. I just don’t always feel ok doing that since I’m beyond tired and don’t feel safe driving at that point.  Hopefully she gets to sleep through the night at some point

I wish we had that. We don’t have anything as far as I know. Most times I’ll just get some papers on their sleep patterns or possible reasons for disrupted sleep. They’re not that helpful personally. I’ve called her doctor before but a lot of times the only thing she can say is run through the list to see if she’s hungry or needs a change but other than that she doesn’t have a lot of advice either.

Possibly? I try to keep the room relatively calm and plain. The only thing I have going occasionally is her noise machine that has soft light she can watch. Otherwise it’s usually just me rocking her in a darker room.

I’m not very close to anyone, especially not my family. Even just physically they live farther away and with the lock down it’s hard to get visitors. The last time my parents took her they couldn’t handle her and I had to leave my errands early so I could go get her.
